what: Baker Hughes supplies equipment and services to energy companies. One half serves oil and gas drilling and production; the other, called Industrial and Energy Technology, makes gas turbines and compressors used in liquefied natural gas plants and increasingly in data centre power.
customers: Oil and gas producers, LNG plant developers, refiners, and industrial and power customers.
money: drilling, completions, production and subsea equipment
gas turbines, compressors and industrial control systems
moat: Turbomachinery for liquefied natural gas plants, where only a handful of companies in the world can supply the compressors, and each plant then needs decades of service.
risks: Oilfield activity has been flat as producers hold spending
Debt of about $18 billion against $4 billion of cash
Large equipment orders are lumpy and can shift between years
Revenue was roughly flat last year
opportunities: Analysts see about 45% upside from current levels
Liquefied natural gas plant construction is in a multi-year build cycle
Gas turbines are now being sold for data centre power, a new market
watch: Industrial and Energy Technology orders and backlog.
